title: Dedicated Unit Economics Model (v1) — Gross Margin by Tier/Shape
content:
Purpose
- Finance model to estimate monthly gross margin (GM) for Redwood Dedicated offers, by Tier (Standard/Plus/Premium) and Hardware Shape, inclusive of:
  - GPU/infra COGS (incl. region adjustments)
  - headroom / spare policy (tier-dependent)
  - burst capacity reserve allocation
  - support + oncall allocations (tier-dependent)
- This sheet is used to validate list pricing bands + discount floors and to sanity-check tier entitlements against GM targets.

Scope / what this is NOT
- Not a per-customer P&L; assumes a standardized “shape” purchase with a typical workload mix.
- Not a throughput model; tokens/sec assumptions only appear to size headroom and burst reserve.

Key outputs (Base Case)
- Standard: target 55–65% GM at list with modest discounting tolerance.
- Plus: target 60–70% GM at list with tighter discounting than Standard due to higher entitlements.
- Premium: target 65–75% GM at list; limited discounting; must be protected by provisioning policy (warm pool + spares).

Model versioning
- v1.0: first pass aligned to Dedicated Tier v1 definitions + current fleet cost assumptions.
- Changes since 2025-03-12: updated H100 $/GPU-hour in us-east; increased Premium support allocation; added “burst pool tax” line item.

=====================================================================
SECTION A — Assumptions (Inputs)

A1) Regions included
| Region code | Notes |
|---|---|
| us-east | primary Dedicated region; broadest shape availability |
| us-west | constrained H100 supply; higher network egress costs |
| eu-west | higher colo + power cost multiplier |

A2) GPU infra costs (blended, fully loaded)
Notes:
- These are all-in costs for finance modeling (hardware lease/depr + power + rack/colo + base ops). Not the raw cloud spot price.
- Fleet provides updates monthly; finance locks for pricing windows.

| GPU type | Cost ($/GPU-hour) us-east | us-west multiplier | eu-west multiplier | Comments |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| L40S 48GB | 1.25 | 1.05 | 1.10 | best availability; good for mid-tier |
| A100 80GB | 2.10 | 1.08 | 1.12 | stable supply; baseline Dedicated shape |
| H100 80GB | 3.85 | 1.12 | 1.15 | supply constrained; procurement risk |

A3) Non-GPU node overhead (per node-month)
Assumes 8x GPU per node shapes (see Section B).

| Line item | $/node-month | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| CPU/RAM + local NVMe | 1,250 | includes host lease + amortized spares |
| Network fabric allocation | 900 | NICs + ToR allocation |
| Base infra ops (non-tiered) | 600 | monitoring, patching, baseline oncall |
| Total non-GPU overhead | 2,750 | add to GPU cost |

A4) Tier entitlements that drive cost

| Tier | Headroom policy (spare) | Warm pool | Burst reserve allocation | Support/oncall intensity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Standard | 15% headroom | none | 5% | business hours + best-effort |
| Plus | 25% headroom | limited (regional) | 8% | faster response, proactive monitoring |
| Premium | 35% headroom | required | 12% | 24/7 + incident comms + credits process |

A5) Utilization assumptions (steady state)
Interpretation:
- “Billable utilization” = portion of committed capacity we expect customer to actually consume.
- For Dedicated, unused committed capacity still bills, but low utilization increases Redwood’s ability to re-use capacity (NOT assumed in v1; conservative).

| Tier | Billable utilization (proxy) | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Standard | 70% | smaller teams, more spiky |
| Plus | 75% | more consistent workloads |
| Premium | 80% | highest steady load; largest deals |

A6) Support cost allocations (per deployment-month)
Allocated cost = blended support labor + SRE incident load attributed to Dedicated tiers.

| Tier | Support allocation $/month | Rationale |
|---|---:|---|
| Standard | 1,250 | shared queue + limited reporting |
| Plus | 2,250 | more frequent perf investigations |
| Premium | 4,500 | 24/7 escalation readiness + customer comms |

A7) Target GM guardrails (policy)
| Tier | GM target @ list | “Do not go below” GM (approval needed) | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Standard | >= 60% | 50% | deal desk if below |
| Plus | >= 65% | 55% | deal desk if below |
| Premium | >= 70% | 60% | exec approval if below |

=====================================================================
SECTION B — Shape Catalog (Finance view)

B1) Standardized shapes (8x GPU nodes)
| Shape code | GPUs | GPU type | CPU/RAM class | Storage | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| rd-ded-l40s-8 | 8 | L40S 48GB | 2x64c / 512GB | 2x3.84TB NVMe | cost-efficient, lower ceiling |
| rd-ded-a100-8 | 8 | A100 80GB | 2x64c / 1TB | 2x3.84TB NVMe | default Dedicated baseline |
| rd-ded-h100-8 | 8 | H100 80GB | 2x96c / 1.5TB | 2x7.68TB NVMe | premium perf / supply limited |

B2) Regional availability (as of 2025-04-01)
| Shape | us-east | us-west | eu-west | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| rd-ded-l40s-8 | GA | GA | GA | broad availability |
| rd-ded-a100-8 | GA | GA | GA | stable lead times |
| rd-ded-h100-8 | Limited | Constrained | Limited | provisioning lead times vary |

=====================================================================
SECTION C — Pricing Inputs (List price bands)

C1) Proposed list price per node-month (by tier)
Notes:
- Plus/Premium include entitlements and higher headroom assumptions; pricing must cover the policy.
- Premium pricing assumes dedicated warm pool + spares are actually enforced (see Section E risks).

| Shape | Standard list $/mo | Plus list $/mo | Premium list $/mo |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| rd-ded-l40s-8 | 19,000 | 22,500 | 27,500 |
| rd-ded-a100-8 | 33,000 | 39,500 | 48,000 |
| rd-ded-h100-8 | 57,500 | 68,500 | 82,500 |

C2) Discounting scenarios (applied to list)
| Scenario | Discount % | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| None | 0% | list |
| Typical | 10% | common annual prepay |
| Aggressive | 20% | deal desk by default |
| Exception | 30% | exec approval + multi-year required |

=====================================================================
SECTION D — COGS Calculation (per node-month)

Definitions
- GPU monthly cost = $/GPU-hour * 24 * 30 * GPU_count * region_multiplier
- Total infra cost = GPU monthly cost + non-GPU overhead
- Effective cost (tier) = Total infra cost * (1 + headroom%)
- Burst reserve tax (tier) = Total infra cost * burst_reserve%
- Tier COGS = Effective cost (tier) + Burst reserve tax (tier) + Support allocation

D1) Base infra cost per node-month (us-east)
| Shape | GPU monthly cost | Non-GPU overhead | Total infra cost |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| rd-ded-l40s-8 | 1.25*720*8 = 7,200 | 2,750 | 9,950 |
| rd-ded-a100-8 | 2.10*720*8 = 12,096 | 2,750 | 14,846 |
| rd-ded-h100-8 | 3.85*720*8 = 22,176 | 2,750 | 24,926 |

D2) Tiered cost adders (us-east)
| Tier | Headroom % | Burst reserve % | Support $ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Standard | 15% | 5% | 1,250 |
| Plus | 25% | 8% | 2,250 |
| Premium | 35% | 12% | 4,500 |

D3) Example calculation (rd-ded-a100-8, us-east)
- Total infra cost = 14,846
- Standard effective cost = 14,846 * 1.15 = 17,073
- Standard burst tax = 14,846 * 0.05 = 742
- Standard tier COGS = 17,073 + 742 + 1,250 = 19,065

=====================================================================
SECTION E — Gross Margin Results (Base Case)

E1) GM by shape/tier (us-east, 0% discount)
GM = 1 - (Tier COGS / Price)

| Shape | Tier | Price $/mo | Tier COGS $/mo | GM % |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| rd-ded-l40s-8 | Standard | 19,000 | (9,950*1.15)+(9,950*0.05)+1,250 = 13,192 | 30.6% |
| rd-ded-l40s-8 | Plus | 22,500 | (9,950*1.25)+(9,950*0.08)+2,250 = 15,681 | 30.3% |
| rd-ded-l40s-8 | Premium | 27,500 | (9,950*1.35)+(9,950*0.12)+4,500 = 19,122 | 30.5% |
| rd-ded-a100-8 | Standard | 33,000 | 19,065 | 42.2% |
| rd-ded-a100-8 | Plus | 39,500 | (14,846*1.25)+(14,846*0.08)+2,250 = 22,815 | 42.2% |
| rd-ded-a100-8 | Premium | 48,000 | (14,846*1.35)+(14,846*0.12)+4,500 = 26,850 | 44.1% |
| rd-ded-h100-8 | Standard | 57,500 | (24,926*1.15)+(24,926*0.05)+1,250 = 31,165 | 45.8% |
| rd-ded-h100-8 | Plus | 68,500 | (24,926*1.25)+(24,926*0.08)+2,250 = 35,386 | 48.3% |
| rd-ded-h100-8 | Premium | 82,500 | (24,926*1.35)+(24,926*0.12)+4,500 = 41,854 | 49.3% |

Interpretation (us-east)
- Current list bands under-hit stated GM targets in Section A7, especially for L40S shapes.
- Even A100/H100 are < 60% GM under the conservative headroom+burst+support model.
- This may be acceptable if we (a) assume some capacity reuse/overbooking beyond a single tenant node, (b) reduce headroom/burst policy in practice, or (c) increase list prices.
- Action: revisit A7 targets OR pricing bands; align with Infra on what “headroom” means (spare nodes vs reserved GPU slices).

E2) Regional sensitivity (A100 Standard, 0% discount)
| Region | Multiplier | Total infra cost | Tier COGS (Standard) | Price | GM |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| us-east | 1.00 | 14,846 | 19,065 | 33,000 | 42.2% |
| us-west | 1.08 (GPU) | 15,814 (approx) | 20,254 (approx) | 33,000 | 38.6% |
| eu-west | 1.12 (GPU) | 16,475 (approx) | 21,116 (approx) | 33,000 | 36.0% |

Notes
- Regional pricing premiums likely required (or region-specific discount floors).
- Alternatively: restrict certain tiers/shapes in higher-cost regions until utilization improves.

=====================================================================
SECTION F — Discount & Burst Stress Tests

F1) Discount sensitivity (A100 Plus, us-east)
| Discount | Net price | Tier COGS | GM |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0% | 39,500 | 22,815 | 42.2% |
| 10% | 35,550 | 22,815 | 35.8% |
| 20% | 31,600 | 22,815 | 27.8% |
| 30% | 27,650 | 22,815 | 17.5% |

F2) Burst reserve stress (Premium, A100, us-east)
Holding headroom/support constant; varying burst reserve.
| Burst reserve % | Tier COGS | GM @ $48,000 |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 8% | (14,846*1.35)+(14,846*0.08)+4,500 = 26,256 | 45.3% |
| 12% (base) | 26,850 | 44.1% |
| 18% | (14,846*1.35)+(14,846*0.18)+4,500 = 27,741 | 42.2% |

F3) Headroom stress (Standard, H100, us-east)
| Headroom % | Tier COGS | GM @ $57,500 |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 10% | (24,926*1.10)+(24,926*0.05)+1,250 = 29,919 | 47.9% |
| 15% (base) | 31,165 | 45.8% |
| 20% | (24,926*1.20)+(24,926*0.05)+1,250 = 32,411 | 43.6% |

=====================================================================
SECTION G — Recommended actions / proposals for v1 launch

G1) Pricing band recommendations (if we hold A4 tier entitlements constant)
- L40S shapes: increase list prices materially OR do not sell Premium on L40S except as a temporary bridge (supply-driven).
- A100 shapes: modest increase (+10–20%) OR explicitly allow capacity reuse accounting (see G3).
- H100 shapes: closer to acceptable but still below target if A7 targets remain; recommend tighter discount floors and explicit regional premiums.

G2) Discount guardrails (proposal)
- Standard:
  - Up to 10%: AE approval
  - 10–20%: Deal Desk required
  - >20%: VP Sales + Finance approval
- Plus:
  - Up to 10%: Deal Desk required
  - >10%: Finance approval; require annual prepay
- Premium:
  - Any discount: Finance approval
  - >10%: exec approval; require multi-year + prepay

G3) Accounting clarification needed (blocking for final GM targets)
Open question: does “headroom %” represent
(a) dedicated spare GPUs reserved for that customer (pure cost), OR
(b) fleet-level spare capacity pooled within a tier/region that can be shared (lower effective cost)?

If (b), we should model headroom and burst reserve as pooled costs, allocated across a tier cohort (reduces per-deployment COGS).

=====================================================================
SECTION H — Open questions / risks

1) Overbooking policy vs Dedicated contract language
- If we treat Dedicated as ‘physically isolated node’ for all tiers, GM is structurally low without large price increases.
- If we treat Dedicated as ‘dedicated pool with policy isolation’, we can achieve GM targets but must align with Legal + SLO wording.

2) H100 supply constraints
- us-west + eu-west H100 procurement risk could increase effective $/GPU-hour and extend warm pool requirements.

3) Support allocations
- Premium support cost is a major driver. If SRE/CS can reduce incident load through better dashboards + runbooks, Premium becomes more viable.

4) Burst pool sizing
- Product wants clear burst entitlements; Infra wants strict caps to protect fleet. Finance needs a stable reserve % assumption and a metering-backed feedback loop.

=====================================================================
Appendix — Notes from reviews
- 2025-03-18: Laura (Finance) flagged that A7 GM targets are inconsistent with current list prices; requested either (a) reprice, or (b) formally adopt pooled accounting.
- 2025-03-27: Vanessa (Fleet) asked to separate ‘warm pool’ cost from ‘headroom’ since warm pool may be regional not per-customer.
- 2025-04-02: Lauren (PM) requested a simplified 1-page summary for exec review (pull from Sections E + G + H).
